blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner. Our approach extracts compact latent actions from the video model's rich spatiotemporal features, compressing each latent video frame by $\boldsymbol{300\times}$ ($\boldsymbol{1{,}200 \rightarrow 4}$ tokens). In addition, by leveraging the video model's generative prior, these latent actions capture action-relevant dynamics disentangled from visual appearance. The resulting latent space serves as a shared action interface across embodiments (human and robot), environments, and action parameterizations. On LARY-Bench, DreamX achieves state-of-the-art performance among latent action models. Moreover, actions encoded in one setting remain effective in another: the latent space supports any-to-any video transfer and zero-shot action transfer across diverse embodiments and environments. Furthermore, this shared interface also enables policy learning in a compact latent action space, reducing the computational cost of video-diffusion-based policies.
blocks.zh: 从录像中学习普遍的行动表现需要建立模型,在对同一行动的不同处决中保持一致,但对表现和外表的变化却无动于衷。 现有的潜伏行动模型推断出视觉过渡中的行动,但其表现往往以无关的视觉变异缠绕了内在行动,限制了跨表征的转移. 我们引入了DreamX,它重新将一个经过预先训练的视频传播模型作为通用的潜在动作学习者. 我们的方法从视频模型丰富的spatiotal特性中提取出紧凑的潜在动作,用$\boldsymbol{300\times}$(\boldsymbol{1{,}200\rightarrow 4}$符来压缩每个潜在的视频框。 此外,通过利用视频模型的先基因,这些潜在动作捕捉与视觉外观脱节的动作相关动态. 由此产生的潜在空间充当了跨越(人和机器人)、环境和行动参数化的共同行动界面。 在LARY-Bench上,DreamX在潜在行动模型中实现了最先进的性能. 此外,在一个背景下编码的行动在另一个背景下依然有效:潜在的空间支持任何到任何视频传输和跨越不同表现和环境的零镜头动作传输。 此外,这一共享界面还使政策学习能够在一个紧凑的潜在行动空间中进行,从而降低基于视频传播的政策的计算成本。

Compact, embodiment-agnostic latent actions extracted from a pretrained video diffusion model capture motion consistently across changes in embodiment and scene appearance. blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Generalist robot policies, including vision-language-action (VLA) models ( Kim et al., 2024 ; Bjorck et al., 2025 ; Intelligence et al., 2025 ) and world action models (WAMs) ( Kim et al., 2026b ; Ye et al., 2026 ) , benefit from diverse robot demonstrations, but collecting such data at scale remains costly.
Human egocentric videos offer a promising alternative as a scalable source of diverse manipulation behaviors, and recent works leverage these videos for policy learning ( Li et al., 2025 ; Kareer et al., 2025 ) .
However, action supervision remains tied to the embodiment that produces it.
Human videos lack robot action labels, and even robot demonstrations use different control spaces across embodiments.
The same behavior can therefore correspond to different low-level actions, making action labels difficult to share directly across embodiments.
Overcoming this mismatch calls for a common action representation that preserves shared motion and effects across embodiments.
blocks.zh:
通用机器人政策,包括视觉语言行动模型(Kim等,2024;Bjorck等,2025;Intelligence等,2025)和世界行动模型(WAMS)(Kim等,2026b; Ye等人,2026年),受益于各种机器人演示,但大规模地收集此类数据仍然代价高昂.
以人类自我为中心的视频提供了一个有希望的替代方案,作为各种操纵行为的可扩展来源,而近期的作品将这些视频用于政策学习(Li等,2025;Kareer等,2025)。
然而,行动监督仍然与产生它的表现有关。
人类的视频缺乏机器人动作标签,甚至机器人的演示也使用不同的控制空间来跨出浮雕.
因此,同一种行为可以对应不同的低级动作,使得动作标签难以直接跨相通.
克服这种不匹配现象,需要有一个共同的行动代表,以保持共同的行动和影响。

blocks.en:
Latent action models (LAMs) offer a promising route toward learning such a representation from video.
Although humans and robots have different bodies and control spaces, their actions can all be observed as changes in a visual scene.
LAMs typically use dedicated encoders to compress these changes into compact representations, called latent actions ( Ye et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2025c ; Bu et al., 2025b ) , where these encoders are trained using a decoder that reconstructs future frames solely from the current frame and latent actions. However, reconstruction accuracy alone does not ensure that latent actions isolate the underlying action. The learned representations can also encode domain-specific visual information, such as viewpoint and scene appearance, whenever it helps reconstruction ( Nikulin et al., 2025 ) . Capturing action-relevant structure shared across embodiments while separating it from domain-specific visual factors therefore remains a challenge.
blocks.zh:
低级行动模式为从视频中学习这种表现提供了一条很有希望的道路。
虽然人类和机器人有不同的身体和控制空间,但是他们的行为都可以作为视觉场景的变化来观察.
LAMs一般使用专用编码器来将这些变化压缩成紧凑的表示,称为"潜在动作"(Ye等,2025;Chen等,2025c;Bu等,2025b),在这些编码器的培训中,使用一个完全从当前框架和潜在动作重建未来框架的解码器. 然而,光靠重建的准确性并不能确保潜在的行动孤立根本行动。 所学的表达方式也可以在任何有助于重建的地方编码特定域的视觉信息,如视角和场景外观(Nikulin等,2025年). 因此,掌握各表现体共享的与行动有关的结构,同时将其与特定领域视觉因素相区分,仍然是一个挑战。

blocks.en:
Pretrained video diffusion models provide a promising foundation for addressing this challenge.
First, through large-scale video generation, they learn rich spatiotemporal representations that capture motion, correspondence, geometry, and semantic structure ( Nam et al., 2026 ; Wiedemer et al., 2025 ; Son et al., 2025 ) .
Such representations encode how scenes, objects, and agents evolve over time, making them a natural source of action-relevant dynamics.
Second, these models possess a generative prior that enables future-frame synthesis conditioned on an initial frame and an additional signal.
With scene appearance supplied by the initial frame, additional conditioning can guide how the scene evolves. Together, these priors motivate extracting latent actions directly from pretrained spatiotemporal representations and supervising their learning with a pretrained generative decoder.
blocks.zh:
事先经过培训的视频传播模式为应对这一挑战提供了一个有希望的基础。
首先,通过大规模视频生成,他们学会了丰富的spatiotal表达,能够捕捉运动,函授,几何和语义结构(Nam等,2026;Wiedemer等,2025;Son等,2025.).
这种表述编码了场景、物体和物剂如何随时间演变,使其成为与行动有关的动态的自然来源。
第二,这些模型具有先入后出,使未来框架合成具有初始框架和额外信号的条件。
随着场景外观由初始框架提供,额外的调制可以指导场景的发展. 这些前科共同激发了直接取出从被预先训练的瞬间表现中潜入的动作,并用经过预先训练的基因解码器监督他们的学习.

blocks.en:
We introduce DreamX , a framework for learning universal latent actions across embodiments using a pretrained video diffusion model. We pass learnable query tokens alongside the video tokens through the model’s spatiotemporal attention, allowing the queries to gather action-relevant information across frames.
The queries condense frame-to-frame changes represented by 1,200 frame tokens into just 4 latent-action tokens, yielding a 𝟑𝟎𝟎 × \mathbf{300\times} reduction in token count. These latent actions replace text conditioning in the same model to reconstruct future frames from the initial frame. With scene appearance supplied by the initial frame and visual detail by the pretrained generative prior, the reconstruction objective encourages latent actions to capture the motion needed to explain the observed future.
blocks.zh:
我们介绍DreamX,这是一个利用事先经过训练的视频传播模式,在各种表现形式中学习普遍潜在行动的框架。 我们通过该模型的瞬间注意力,将可学习的查询符和视频符一起传递,使查询能够收集跨帧的与行动有关的信息。
查询将1,200个帧符号表示的帧到帧变化压缩成4个潜在动作符号,从而产生300 ×\ mathbf{300\times} 符号计数的减少。 这些潜在动作取代了同一模型中的文本条件,以从初始框架重建未来框架. 由于场景的外观由初始框架提供,而视觉细节则由事先受过训练的遗传学前人提供,因此重建目标鼓励潜在的行动来捕捉解释所观察到的未来所需的运动.

blocks.en: Trained on heterogeneous human and robot videos, DreamX achieves state-of-the-art performance among latent action models on LARYBench ( Nie et al., 2026 ) and enables any-to-any video transfer and human-to-robot action transfer without paired training data. As a downstream application, we also show that the learned latent actions can serve as prediction targets for an observation-conditioned robot policy, without requiring future-video generation during execution. Together, these results suggest that DreamX learns a shared, transferable latent action space that supports motion transfer across embodiments and can also serve as a basis for downstream policy learning.
blocks.zh: DreamX在LARY Bench(Nie等人,2026年)的潜在行动模型中进行了关于人与机器人不同视频的培训,实现了最先进的性能,并使得任何视频传输和人与机器人的动作传输都无需配对培训数据。 作为一种下游应用,我们还表明,所学到的潜在行动可以作为观察条件机器人政策的预测目标,而无需在执行过程中产生未来视频。 这些结果共同表明,DreamX学习了一个共享的、可转移的潜在行动空间,支持运动的跨化转移,也可以作为下游政策学习的基础。

blocks.en: In summary, our contributions are as follows: • We introduce DreamX, a framework that uses the spatiotemporal and generative priors of a pretrained video diffusion model to learn universal latent actions. The resulting representations achieve state-of-the-art performance among latent action models on LARYBench. • We demonstrate that the learned latent space supports any-to-any video transfer and human-to-robot action transfer without paired source–target training data. We further show the use of compact latent-action codes as prediction targets for downstream policy learning.
blocks.zh: 简言之,我们的贡献如下: 我们引入了DreamX, 这个框架使用一个预先训练的视频传播模型的先导和先导, 来学习普遍的潜伏动作。 由此产生的说明在LARY Bench的潜在行动模式中取得了最新业绩。 我们证明,所学到的潜在空间支持任何视频传输和人对机器人动作传输,而不提供对称源-目标培训数据。 我们进一步表明,利用紧凑的潜在行动守则作为下游政策学习的预测目标。

blocks.en: We introduce DreamX, a framework that uses the spatiotemporal and generative priors of a pretrained video diffusion model to learn universal latent actions. The resulting representations achieve state-of-the-art performance among latent action models on LARYBench.

blocks.en: 2 Related Works
blocks.zh: 2 相关工程

blocks.en: Latent action models (LAMs) learn action representations from visual transitions, enabling action-unlabeled videos to supervise downstream control. LAPO ( Schmidt and Jiang, 2024 ) and Genie ( Bruce et al., 2024 ) established the paradigm, recovering discrete latent actions through an inverse–forward dynamics bottleneck over adjacent frames. LAPA ( Ye et al., 2025 ) further scales this recipe for vision-language-action pretraining, and Moto ( Chen et al., 2025c ) tokenizes visual motion for manipulation. Later work incorporates additional cues: UniVLA ( Bu et al., 2025b ) grounds latent actions with semantic visual features, villa-X ( Chen et al., 2025b ) integrates language and robot-state dynamics, and CoMo ( Yang et al., 2026 ) and DiLA ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) separate motion from visual content. Across these variants, the action space is learned from scratch on a local visual transition, often a single frame pair. Such supervision offers no view of how motion persists beyond one step, so the encoder entangles action with appearance and yields representations tied to their training embodiments.
blocks.zh: Latement动作模型(LAMS)从视觉过渡中学习动作表现,使动作无标签的视频能够监督下游控制. LAPO(Smidt and Jiang, 2024年)和Genie(Bruce等, 2024年)建立了这一范式,通过相邻框架的反向动态瓶颈来恢复离散的潜在行动。 LAPA(Ye等,2025年)进一步标出这种用于视觉语言动作预训的配方,而Moto(Chen等,2025年c)则将视觉运动作为操纵的象征. 后一作品还包含了额外的提示:UniVLA(Bu等,2025年b)为具有语义视觉特征的潜伏动作作由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来由来相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相 在这些变体中,动作空间是从局部视觉过渡中从零开始学习的,往往是一对相框. 这种监督无法说明运动是如何持续到一步之后的,因此编码器将动作与外表相缠并产生与训练相接的表述。

blocks.en: Video generative models acquire spatiotemporal structure by modeling how scenes evolve over time. Their internal representations support correspondence, point tracking, optical flow, and geometric understanding without task-specific supervision ( Nam et al., 2026 ; Vélez et al., 2025 ; Vedder et al., 2024 ; Huang et al., 2025 ) , and text-conditioned models further exhibit semantic grounding over objects, behaviors, and interactions ( Wiedemer et al., 2025 ) . Rather than encoding physical laws explicitly, these representations capture motion, geometry, and semantics jointly: which entities are present, where they are, and how they move over time. This is precisely the composition a latent action must express, which is a structured change of a specific entity in a specific place, and it is acquired from web-scale video rather than from a single frame pair.
blocks.zh: 视频基因模型通过模拟场景如何随时间演变而获得spatiotopal结构. 其内部表述支持通信、点跟踪、光学流动和几何理解,而不进行特定任务监督(Nam等,2026;Vélez等,2025;Vedder等,2024;Huang等,2025;和文字条件模型进一步显示对物体、行为和相互作用的语义定位(Wiedemer等,2025)。 这些表达法不是明确地编码物理定律,而是共同捕捉运动,几何和语义:哪些实体存在,它们在哪里,以及它们如何随时间而移动. 这恰恰是潜在动作必须表达的构成,这是特定地点特定实体的结构化变化,它从网络尺度的视频而不是从一对相框中获得.

blocks.en: Recent work connects these two lines. VPP ( Hu et al., 2024 ) conditions a manipulation policy on the predictive visual representations inside a fine-tuned video diffusion model, but still learns the policy from action labels. AdaWorld ( Gao et al., 2025 ) learns latent actions for adaptable video prediction, and VideoWorld2 ( Ren et al., 2026b ) pairs a pretrained video diffusion model for generation with a separate latent dynamics model. In both, the video model acts as a generative prior supplying pixels or rollouts, while the action representation is produced by an external module trained from scratch on frame-level transitions. Thus, the latent action encoder does not directly read the video diffusion backbone’s internal representations. We instead read latent actions directly from the model’s rich spatiotemporal representation, making maximal use of video pretraining and requiring no per-embodiment action encoder.
blocks.zh: 最近的工作将这两行连接起来. VPP(Hu等,2024年)在微调视频传播模型内对预测视觉表现设定了操纵政策,但仍从动作标签中学习了这一政策. AdaWorld(Gao等,2025年)学习了可适应的视频预测的潜在动作,而VideoWorld2(Ren等,2026年b)为一代人搭配了一个经过预先训练的视频传播模型,并配有单独的潜伏动态模型. 在两者中,视频模型都起到先基因后基因提供像素或推出等效物的作用,而动作表现则由从头到尾接受帧级过渡培训的外部模块来制作. 因此,潜在动作编码器不会直接读取视频传播主干线的内部表述. 相反,我们直接从模型丰富的瞬间表现中读取潜在的动作,最大限度地利用视频预训,不需要每个化身动作编码器。

blocks.en: Figure 2: DreamX architecture and attention masks. (a) Learnable queries read out the pretrained video backbone’s spatiotemporal representations to encode latent actions. A decoder initialized from the same pretrained backbone reconstructs future video from the latent actions and the initial frame, with auxiliary action supervision when labels are available. (b) Encoder and decoder attention masks control information flow among video, query, and action tokens. In the decoder, video and action tokens read the latent-action queries but do not attend to one another.

blocks.en: Given a video and instruction, DreamX uses learnable queries to extract compact latent actions from a pretrained video diffusion backbone’s spatiotemporal features. Future-frame reconstruction conditioned on these latent actions and the initial frame provides generative supervision (Sec. 3.2 ). The learned representation enables video and action transfer with a target initial frame or robot state (Sec. 3.3 ). For control, the DreamX policy predicts compact codes and low-level actions without generating future video (Sec. 3.4 ).

blocks.en: 3.2 Learning Universal Latent Actions from Video Diffusion Priors
blocks.zh: 3.2 从视频传播前科中学习通用后期动作

blocks.en: DreamX adapts a pretrained video diffusion backbone for two complementary roles: encoding observed dynamics into latent actions and supervising them through future-frame reconstruction to encourage separation of motion from visual appearance. Building on Sec. 3.1 , we introduce learnable queries that read out the video representations to summarize observed dynamics as latent actions, while the decoder reconstructs the future from these latent actions and the initial frame. Leveraging a video diffusion backbone for both the encoder and decoder allows its generative prior to account for visual appearance, encouraging the latent action tokens to focus on motion.
blocks.zh: DreamX为两个互补角色调整了预先训练的视频传播主干线:将所观察到的动态编码为潜在动作,并通过未来框架重建对其进行监督,以鼓励运动与视觉外观分离. 以第3.1节为基础,我们提出了可学习的询问,宣读视频表述,总结所观察到的动态作为潜在行动,而解码器则从这些潜在行动和初始框架中重建未来。 利用编码器和解码器的视频传播主干线,可以使其在对视觉外观进行记分前具有基因,鼓励潜在动作符号专注于运动.

blocks.en: 3.3 Motion Transfer via Latent Actions
blocks.zh: 3.3 通过Latent 动作移动

blocks.en: Building upon the rich generative prior from the video diffusion backbone, DreamX learns latent actions that capture motion transferable across embodiments, even though cross-embodiment transfer is not an explicit training objective. This capability emerges from the pretraining described in the previous section and requires no additional training. The auxiliary robot action branch further encourages the latent actions to encode action-relevant cues and further enables motion extracted from a source video to be decoded into continuous actions executable by a target embodiment.
blocks.zh: DreamX借鉴了视频传播主干线上丰富的基因,学习了捕捉跨浮雕可转移运动的潜在动作,尽管交叉浮雕转移并不是一个明确的培训目标. 这一能力来自上一节所述的预训,不需要额外培训。 辅助机器人动作分支进一步鼓励潜在动作编码与动作相关的提示,并进一步使从源视频中提取的动作能被解码为由目标能被执行的连续动作.

blocks.en: 3.4 Policy Learning with Compact Latent Actions
blocks.zh: 3.4 用契约后遗症行动学习政策

blocks.en: As a downstream application, we examine whether the latent actions learned by DreamX can serve as prediction targets for an observation-conditioned robot policy. Whereas motion transfer uses latent actions extracted from a source demonstration, the policy predicts them from the current observation and instruction. To this end, we repurpose the same pretrained video backbone used by DreamX to predict latent actions in place of future video ( Kim et al., 2026a ) . Although Q Q is compact in token count, each token retains the full backbone width, making direct diffusion high-dimensional ( Chen et al., 2025a ) . We therefore compress Q Q into a low-dimensional code Z Z first, which serves as the policy’s prediction target.

blocks.en: 4 Experimental Results
blocks.zh: 4 实验结果

blocks.en: We evaluate whether DreamX learns universal latent actions by examining how well they capture motion (Sec. 4.1 ) and whether they can transfer across scenes and embodiments (Secs. 4.2 – 4.3 ). We further assess their utility for learning effective and efficient policies from human and robot demonstrations (Sec. 4.4 ), followed by ablations and analysis of the learned representation (Secs. 4.5 – 4.6 ).
blocks.zh: 我们评价DreamX是否通过考察它们如何捕捉运动(第4.1节)以及它们是否能够跨越场景和浮雕(第4.2至4.3节)来学习普遍的潜在行动。 我们进一步评估它们对于从人和机器人演示中学习有效和高效政策的效用(第4.4节),然后对所学到的表述(第4.5至4.6节)进行整理和分析。

blocks.en: 4.1 Representation Quality
blocks.zh: 4.1 代表质量

blocks.en: We examine how well DreamX’s latent actions capture motion on LARYBench ( Nie et al., 2026 ) . Regression asks whether the representation retains enough fine-grained motion to recover end-effector trajectories, and classification whether it carries enough semantic information to distinguish different motions. Table 1 compares DreamX with latent action models that encode either frame pairs or video clips. DreamX achieves the best performance across all benchmarks. Compared with the strongest baseline, DiLA, DreamX reduces regression MSE from 0.38 to 0.17 and increases classification accuracy from 62.25% to 69.67%. These results support leveraging video models as a source of action-relevant representations: reading latent actions directly from their pretrained priors yields representations that capture spatial, temporal, and semantic structure across embodiments. FAE-32, our 32-channel compressed representation (Sec. 3.4 ), also outperforms all baselines, indicating that even the compact codes retain substantial motion and semantic information. Further evaluation details are provided in Appendix B.4 .

blocks.en: We evaluate zero-shot human-to-robot transfer on HumanAndRobot ( Xie et al., 2026 ) , comparing with AdaWorld ( Gao et al., 2025 ) and VideoWorld 2 ( Ren et al., 2026b ) , both of which use diffusion-based video decoders. Paired robot recordings serve only as evaluation references; no paired human–robot data is used for training . DreamX outperforms both baselines on every metric in Table 2 and follows the source human motion while preserving the target robot and scene (Figure 5 ). In contrast, AdaWorld exhibits visual degradation in this out-of-distribution setting, while VideoWorld 2 occasionally introduces a human hand despite its appearance-disentangling design. These results suggest that DreamX better separates transferable motion from appearance, enabling more consistent human-to-robot transfer.

blocks.en: 4.3 Action Transfer

blocks.en: We evaluate action transfer to examine whether our latent actions form a universal representation space that connects similar motions across embodiments. Following Sec. 3.3 , we extract latent actions from a human video and decode them into low-level actions for the target robot. Execution is open-loop without visual observations : only the latent actions specify the motion, while proprioception provides the robot’s initial state. Notably, this transfer is learned without paired human–robot training data , so the two embodiments are connected through the shared latent action space. Figure 6 shows that the robot reproduces the stroke structure of the letter “N,” preserving the demonstrated motion beyond a coarse task outcome. In single-arm pushing, it follows the forward-then-left sequence, retaining the direction change and temporal order. Bimanual pushing further shows corresponding movements of both arms, suggesting that the shared latent representation retains arm-specific motion and transfers it to the corresponding robot arms. Evaluation protocols and additional examples are provided in Appendices B.2 and D.2 , respectively.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We present DreamX, a framework that leverages pretrained video diffusion priors to learn universal latent actions. Its spatiotemporal representations provide action-relevant dynamics, while its generative prior supervises latent-action learning through future-frame reconstruction. DreamX achieves state-of-the-art performance among latent action models on LARYBench and enables any-to-any video transfer and human-to-robot action transfer without paired training data. Predicting these compact latent actions also supports effective and efficient policy learning from human and robot demonstrations. Together, these results highlight pretrained video models as a foundation for learning reusable action representations across embodiments.
blocks.zh: 我们介绍DreamX, 这个框架利用预先训练的视频传播前科来学习普遍的潜在行动。 它的瞬间表现提供与行动有关的动态,而它的先天性通过未来框架的重建监督潜在行动学习。 DreamX在LARY Bench上的潜在动作模型中实现了最先进的性能,并使得任何视频传输和人对机器人动作传输都无需配对训练数据. 预测这些紧凑的潜在行动也有助于从人和机器人的演示中有效地学习政策。 这些成果共同突出了经过预先培训的视频模型,作为学习可重复使用的各种表现的基础。

executed open-loop, without visual feedback , conditioned on the human
latent actions and the robot’s initial proprioceptive state.

We evaluate three types of motion transfer. Writing tests whether
latent actions preserve fine-grained spatial trajectories and stroke order;
a marker attached to the right gripper reproduces the demonstrated shape. Single-arm pushing tests whether the representation captures changes
in motion direction and their temporal order, requiring the robot to follow
a forward-then-left sequence. Bimanual manipulation tests whether
latent actions retain arm-specific motion and transfer it to the corresponding
robot arms. Additional examples are provided in
Section D.2 .

移动方向及其时间顺序,要求机器人遵循

only the lower drawer open, and both drawers open, as illustrated in

upper drawer before the lower drawer. A fixed top-view RGB camera observes
the workspace.

blocks.en:
We compare DreamX with Mimic-Video ( Pai et al., 2025 ) , using human videos and
robot demonstrations for task-specific learning. DreamX starts from the
pretrained latent-action generator, while Mimic-Video starts from a video
backbone pretrained on MolmoAct. Each method then incorporates an action head
for task-specific learning, and both are trained for 30,000 steps. For DreamX,
human videos supervise latent-action prediction, while robot demonstrations
additionally supervise low-level actions. During rollout, DreamX generates
compact latent actions alongside low-level actions, whereas Mimic-Video
generates future video.

用于特定任务学习的机器人演示。 梦 X 从

紧凑的潜在行动与低级行动,而模拟影视
生成未来的视频。

blocks.en:
We evaluate reaching and pushing as two subgoals: reaching measures whether
the robot approaches the drawer for interaction, and pushing measures whether
it completes the required closure. The reported subgoal success rate averages
the two completion rates within each configuration, and the overall average
weights the three configurations equally. We additionally report inference
latency per policy call. Separate reaching and pushing results are provided in
Section C.1 .
We collected 45 trajectories to train the policy and evaluated its success rate over 10 trials in each of three scenarios.

blocks.en: B.4 LARYBench Evaluation Details
blocks.zh: B.4 LARY BENCH 评价细节

blocks.en:
We freeze all representation models and train a common attentive probe for
action regression and classification. Each input token is projected to 768
dimensions through a linear layer, layer normalization, and GELU. For
representations spanning multiple transitions, learned temporal embeddings
identify the transition positions before the temporal and token dimensions
are flattened. A learned-query attentive pooler aggregates the tokens into a
single feature for the regression or classification head.
blocks.zh:
我们冻结所有代表模型,并培训一个共同的专注探测器
动作回归和分类。 每个输入令牌预计为768个
维度通过线性层,层态化,和GELU. 对于
跨越多个过渡、学习时间嵌入的表述
在时间和象征层面之前确定过渡立场
被平了下来。 一个有学问的专注的游泳池 将符号集合成一个
回归或分类头的单一特征。

blocks.en:
The regression benchmark originally provides only two frames per sample.
Using the accompanying metadata, we recover the corresponding video sequences
from the source datasets, including the intervening frames, for video-based models.

回归基准最初只提供每个样本的两个框架.
利用附带的元数据,我们恢复相应的视频序列
从源数据集,包括视频模型的干涉帧。

blocks.en:
We extract each model’s native representation without fine-tuning and preserve
its temporal and token structure. Pair-based models encode consecutive frame
pairs, while video-based models encode clips using their supported temporal
windows. Features are precomputed for probe training.
blocks.zh:
我们抽取每个模型的本地代表 而不调整和保存
它的时间和象征结构。 基于对等模式连续编码框架
,而基于视频的模型则使用其支持的时间编码剪辑
窗口。 特征被预先计算用于探测训练.

blocks.en:
We evaluate on 1,008 clips spanning 21 tasks from
HumanAndRobot ( Xie et al., 2026 ) , selecting 48 clips per task.
Each method receives a human source video and the initial frame of its paired
robot recording. The remaining robot frames serve only as evaluation references; no paired human–robot data is used for training . We compare DreamX with
AdaWorld ( Gao et al., 2025 ) and VideoWorld 2 ( Ren et al., 2026b ) using their
native generation horizons.

每种方法都接收到人源视频及其初始配对框架
机器人录音。 其余的机器人帧仅作为评价参考;没有将人-机器人数据配对用于培训。 我们比较DreamX和
AdaWorld(Gao等人,2025年)和VideoWorld 2(Ren等人,2026年b)使用其
本土一代地平线.

For a common evaluation horizon, we retain the first 20 frames of each output
and exclude the conditioning frame, yielding 19 generated frames per clip.
We report FVD using a Kinetics-400-pretrained I3D network, VGG-based LPIPS,
PSNR, and SSIM against the corresponding robot reference videos.
